title: How a 1937 Nobel Paper Predicted Tiny Million-Dollar Firms
alt_title_1: Ronald Coase's 1937 Law Behind One-Person Software Businesses
alt_title_2: Why Shrinking Transaction Costs Favor Tiny High-Margin Teams
description_hook: In 1937, future Nobel laureate Ronald Coase published 'The Nature of the Firm' in Economica, showing that large companies exist only when market transaction costs are high. As software and AI shrink coordination costs, tiny high-margin firms gain a structural edge.

scenes.headline: The 1937 Paper Behind Tiny High-Profit Firms
scenes.stat_label: YEAR RONALD COASE EXPLAINED FIRM SIZE
bullets: Big revenue once required giant internal headcount
One economic variable changed the math
scenes.narration: In 1937, a twenty-six-year-old British economist wrote a paper that quietly explains why tiny one-to-three-person software businesses now rival hundred-person agencies in profit.
scenes.source: Ronald Coase, 'The Nature of the Firm', Economica (1937)

scenes.headline: Ronald Coase's Transaction Cost Discovery
scenes.stat_label: FIRMS EXIST TO REDUCE COORDINATION FRICTION
bullets: Hiring external vendors once meant steep search & contract costs
Firms grew only until internal bureaucracy cost just as much
scenes.narration: In Economica, future Nobel laureate Ronald Coase asked why large corporations exist at all. His answer was transaction costs: searching for specialists, negotiating contracts, and policing quality across open markets.
scenes.source: Ronald Coase, 'The Nature of the Firm', Economica (1937); Nobel Prize in Economics (1991)

scenes.headline: Chasing Headcount Status Recreates Bureaucracy
scenes.left_body: 30 employees -> endless status calls & thin net margins
scenes.right_body: 1-3 builders + APIs & AI -> low overhead & calm autonomy
scenes.narration: For eighty years, high transaction costs forced ambitious founders to hire big internal staffs. Today, many entrepreneurs still chase headcount for status, recreating slow corporate bureaucracy.

scenes.headline: Automate Repeatable Work Before Hiring
scenes.stat_label: LOWER TRANSACTION COSTS -> SMALLER OPTIMAL TEAMS
scenes.stat_subtext: APIs + scripts + AI shrink coordination overhead
scenes.narration: Modern APIs, cloud billing, and AI workflows collapse coordination friction. Build Coasean micro-firms instead: keep core ownership tiny and automate repeatable production before hiring anyone.

scenes.headline: Optimize Profit Per Person, Not Office Size
bullets: Replace repetitive admin with deterministic code
Judge success by free cashflow and unscheduled hours
scenes.narration: Measure your business by free cashflow and calm calendar hours per person, never by crowded office headcount.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin application of Ronald Coase, Economica (1937)
